title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover & load-shedding
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: During last week's incident (INC-4319) we observed the SLO enforcer enter a tight backoff ordering loop when multiple regions simultaneously triggered load-shedding and failover. The root cause was a race between the backoff queue reordering logic and the regional failover state transitions which allowed earlier requests to be re-enqueued ahead of later ones, causing hysteresis to be bypassed and triggering repeated cross-region failovers.

This PR: deterministic ordering + stability guards. Summary of changes: 1) Replace opportunistic reordering with monotonic enqueue sequence numbers to ensure deterministic backoff ordering across nodes; 2) Add a hysteresis timer and minimum backoff interval to prevent re-triggering failover within a short window; 3) Add a regional failover throttle that rate-limits failover decisions when load-shedding is active; 4) Harden state transitions in the SLO enforcer state machine to avoid duplicate in-flight failover decisions; 5) Add unit and integration tests reproducing the race; 6) Expose new metrics and a short-lived debug log gate for canary rollouts.

Why this approach: deterministic ordering (sequence numbers + compare-with-timestamp) avoids nondeterministic reordering while keeping the backoff optimization intact. Hysteresis + throttle prevents thrashing when upstream capacity fluctuates rapidly. The changes are narrowly scoped to the enforcer and failover orchestration code to minimize blast radius.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduce race locally with synthetic workload harness - [x] Add unit tests for enqueue ordering and hysteresis - [x] Integration test: simulate multi-region load-shedding -> ensure single failover decision - [x] Metrics and dashboard patches - [x] Canary plan documented below

Impact: fixes observed incident class where regional failover thrashing caused increased latency and risk of cascading capacity melt. No API changes.

b3e5d7a: add hysteresis timer and minimum-backoff-interval config
c4a6f8b: regional failover throttle + guard in state machine
d5b7e9c: add unit/integration tests for ordering and failover behavior
e6c8f0d: add metrics: slo_enforcer.backoff_reorders, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_active, slo_enforcer.failover_throttle_count
f7d9a1e: docs: update observability dashboard and runbook references
release_notes: Patch: Fix race in SLO enforcer backoff ordering that could cause cross-region failover thrashing under load-shedding. Adds hysteresis and a regional failover throttle. Includes metrics and tests.
review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Can we guarantee sequence monotonicity across restarts? If not, add a bootstrap offset.
Aisha Patel: Added bootstrap offset logic and persisted last-seq in the enforcer checkpoint. See commit a1f4c2d.
Priya Singh: Integration test reproduced the issue locally, and this PR prevents the thrash locally. Left one minor nits about timeout values.
Aisha Patel: Addressed timeout nits, added config flags with sensible defaults and made them runtime-configurable.
Jared Kim: Verified metric names and dashboards. Approved after CI green.
notes_on_deploy: Canary deploy to eu-west-1 at 5% traffic for 30 minutes; monitor slo_enforcer.failover_throttle_count and slo_enforcer.hysteresis_active. If stable, expand to us-east-1 and then full rollout. Enable debug logging gate for 2 hours in canary only.
test_plan: Unit tests added. Integration harness simulates multi-region load-shedding and asserts a single failover decision. Canary with synthetic traffic reproducing the incident pattern. Post-deploy: monitor dashboard and PagerDuty channel for 1 hour after full rollout.
notes: This is a narrowly scoped hotfix; long-term we will evaluate a global sequencer service for enforcer ordering (ENG-2521).
